source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֞ע שְׁפַטְיָ֣ה בֶן־מַתָּ֗ן וּגְדַלְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן־פַּשְׁח֔וּר וְיוּכַל֙ בֶּן־שֶׁ֣לֶמְיָ֔הוּ וּפַשְׁח֖וּר בֶּן־מַלְכִּיָּ֑ה אֶ֨ת־הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֧ר יִרְמְיָ֛הוּ מְדַבֵּ֥ר אֶל־כָּל־הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And heard Shephatiah son of Mattan and Gedaliah son of Pashhur and Jucal son of Shelemiah and Pashhur son of Malchiah the words that Jeremiah [was] speaking to all the people, saying,

en.L: And Shephatiah son of Mattan and Gedaliah son of Pashhur and Jucal son of Shelemiah and Pashhur son of Malchiah heard the words that Jeremiah was speaking to all the people, saying,
en.B: Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jucal son of Shelemiah and Pashhur son of Malchiah heard what Jeremiah was saying to all the people:
en.R: Four of the king's leaders heard the message Jeremiah was giving to all the people. They were Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jucal son of Shelemiah and Pashhur son of Malchiah. Jeremiah was saying,

decisions.choice: Jucal son of Shelemiah: the same man as Jehucal son of Shelemiah in 37:3
decisions.reason: In 37:3 King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah to ask Jeremiah to pray for the city. Jucal is a shorter form of the same name, and the father's name matches. The man the king once sent to the prophet now joins those who want him dead.

decisions.choice: Pashhur son of Malchiah: the official of 21:1
decisions.reason: Zedekiah sent this Pashhur to Jeremiah in 21:1. He is a different man from Pashhur son of Immer, the priest who beat Jeremiah (20:1-2).

decisions.choice: Gedaliah son of Pashhur: not the later governor
decisions.reason: This Gedaliah is not Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the Babylonians later made governor and who protected Jeremiah (39:14; 40:5). His father may be Pashhur son of Immer (20:1), but the text does not say.

decisions.choice: was speaking: Jeremiah kept speaking to the people from where he was held
decisions.reason: Jeremiah was confined in the courtyard of the guard (37:21), but people could come to him there (32:2, 12). The form of the verb describes what he was going on doing.

decisions.choice: Four of the king's leaders ... They were
decisions.reason: Readable says first who these men are (verse 4 calls them officials) and then gives their names in a sentence of their own, so the list does not stand before the verb.

source.text: כֹּה֮ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֒ הַיֹּשֵׁב֙ בָּעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את יָמ֕וּת בַּחֶ֖רֶב בָּרָעָ֣ב וּבַדָּ֑בֶר וְהַיֹּצֵ֤א אֶל־הַכַּשְׂדִּים֙ וְחָיָ֔ה וְהָיְתָה־לּ֥וֹ נַפְשׁ֛וֹ לְשָׁלָ֖ל וָחָֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh: The [one] staying in the city this will die by the sword, by the famine and by the pestilence; but the [one] going out to the Chaldeans will live, and will be to him his life for plunder, and he will live.

en.L: "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 'Whoever stays in this city will die by the sword, by the famine and by the pestilence; but whoever goes out to the Chaldeans will live, and his life will be his as plunder, and he will live.'
en.B: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: 'Those who stay in this city will die by sword, famine and plague. But those who go out to the Chaldeans will live; they will come away with their lives as their only plunder, and they will live.'
en.R: "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: 'Anyone who stays in this city will die from war, famine or disease. But anyone who goes out and surrenders to the Babylonians will live. They will escape with their lives, and that will be all they get. Yes, they will live.'

decisions.choice: the saying of 21:9 repeated
decisions.reason: These are almost the words of 21:9. There the one who leaves the city "falls to" the Chaldeans; here he simply "goes out" to them, and the saying ends with "and he will live" a second time.

decisions.choice: his life will be his as plunder: he will escape with his life and nothing more
decisions.reason: As in 21:9: the one who surrenders carries off his own life, as a soldier carries off plunder from a battle. The note at 21:9 gives the other way of reading the picture.

decisions.choice: go out to the Chaldeans: surrender to the besieging army
decisions.reason: To go out of a besieged city to the enemy is to give oneself up to them (verse 17; 21:9; 1 Samuel 11:3).

decisions.choice: will live: the form read aloud, with the same sense as the written form
decisions.reason: As in 21:9, the written Hebrew text has one form of the verb "live" and the margin tells readers to read another, with "and" in front. The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: sword, famine and plague (B); war, famine or disease (R); Babylonians (R)
decisions.reason: The wording settled for Jeremiah, as in 21:9.

decisions.choice: those who ... they (B); anyone who ... they (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "he who" means any person, man or woman. As in 21:9, Balanced uses the plural and Readable "anyone" and "they", so no gender setting is needed.

decisions.choice: goes out and surrenders
decisions.reason: Readable says what going out to the enemy means (m3).

source.text: כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה הִנָּתֹ֨ן תִּנָּתֵ֜ן הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֗את בְּיַ֛ד חֵ֥יל מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל וּלְכָדָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh: Surely will be given the city this into [the] hand of [the] army of [the] king of Babylon, and he will capture it.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 'This city will surely be given into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.'"
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: 'This city will certainly be handed over to the king of Babylon's army, and he will capture it.'"
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: 'This city will surely be handed over to the army of the king of Babylon. He will capture it.'"

decisions.choice: will surely be given: the doubled verb makes the statement certain
decisions.reason: The verb "be given" is repeated, "being given it will be given", to leave no doubt about what will happen (32:3-4; 34:2-3).

decisions.choice: into the hand of: into the power of
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power and control. To be given into an army's hand is to be handed over to it in defeat (21:10).

decisions.choice: handed over to
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "given into the hand of" (m2).

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ הַשָּׂרִ֜ים אֶל־הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ י֣וּמַת נָא֮ אֶת־הָאִ֣ישׁ הַזֶּה֒ כִּֽי־עַל־כֵּ֡ן הֽוּא־מְרַפֵּ֡א אֶת־יְדֵי֩ אַנְשֵׁ֨י הַמִּלְחָמָ֜ה הַֽנִּשְׁאָרִ֣ים׀בָּעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֗את וְאֵת֙ יְדֵ֣י כָל־הָעָ֔ם לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כַּדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה כִּ֣י׀הָאִ֣ישׁ הַזֶּ֗ה אֵינֶ֨נּוּ דֹרֵ֧שׁ לְשָׁל֛וֹם לָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה כִּ֥י אִם־לְרָעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the princes to the king, Let be put to death please the man this, for therefore he [is] making drop the hands of the men of the war, the [ones] remaining in the city this, and the hands of all the people, by speaking to them according to the words these; for the man this not he [is] seeking for welfare for the people this, but for harm.

en.L: And the princes said to the king, "Let this man be put to death, please, for in this way he is weakening the hands of the men of war who remain in this city, and the hands of all the people, by speaking words like these to them; for this man is not seeking the welfare of this people, but [their] harm."
en.B: Then the officials said to the king, "This man must be put to death. By saying such things he is weakening the resolve of the soldiers who are left in this city, and of all the people as well. This man is not seeking the good of this people, but their harm."
en.R: Then the leaders said to the king, "This man must be put to death! The things he is saying are making the soldiers who are still in this city lose heart, and all the people too. This man does not want what is good for these people. He wants to hurt them."

decisions.choice: weakening the hands: taking away their courage and will to fight
decisions.reason: Hands that drop are hands that can no longer do their work. To make someone's hands drop is to discourage them (Ezra 4:4; Isaiah 35:3). In a city under siege this was a charge of undermining the defense.

decisions.choice: the men of war: the soldiers
decisions.reason: "Men of war" means fighting men, the troops still defending the city.

decisions.choice: welfare: the good and safety of the people
decisions.reason: The word usually rendered "peace" here means well-being as a whole, the people's good and safety, set against "harm". The officials claim Jeremiah wants the city to suffer (compare 29:7, where he tells the exiles to seek the welfare of Babylon).

decisions.choice: for in this way: the reason they give for the death sentence
decisions.reason: The words "for therefore" join the demand to its reason: because of what he says, he is weakening the defenders.

decisions.choice: princes (L); officials (B); leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this word in Jeremiah (1:18). These are the king's chief officers, not his sons.

decisions.choice: weakening the resolve (B); making ... lose heart (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the picture of dropping hands (m1); Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: please left unexpressed
decisions.reason: The officials soften their demand with a polite word, "please". Literal keeps it; in Balanced and Readable "This man must be put to death" carries the demand without it, as a request to the king.

decisions.choice: welfare (L); good (B); what is good (R)
decisions.reason: The sense here is well-being, not the absence of war (m3), so the word "peace" is not used.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֔הוּ הִנֵּה־ה֖וּא בְּיֶדְכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־אֵ֣ין הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יוּכַ֥ל אֶתְכֶ֖ם דָּבָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the king Zedekiah, Look, he [is] in your hand, for not the king is able [to do against] you a thing.

en.L: And King Zedekiah said, "Look, he [is] in your hand, for the king is not able [to do] anything against you."
en.B: King Zedekiah said, "Very well, he is in your hands. The king can do nothing to oppose you."
en.R: King Zedekiah answered, "All right, he is in your power. There is nothing the king can do to stop you."

decisions.choice: in your hand: in your power, yours to deal with
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power and control (26:14). The king gives Jeremiah up to the officials.

decisions.choice: the king can do nothing: the king speaks of himself in the third person
decisions.reason: Zedekiah speaks of "the king" rather than "I". The title only makes his weakness plainer: the king cannot stand up to his own officials. He sought Jeremiah's word in secret (37:17), but in public he does not protect him.

decisions.choice: look: here, take him
decisions.reason: The word that often means "look" here hands something over, giving in to the officials' demand.

decisions.choice: Very well (B); All right (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the force of "look" in this setting (m3).

decisions.choice: in your hands ... to oppose you (B); in your power ... to stop you (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of the hand, Readable gives its sense (m1). Both say what the king cannot do against them.

source.text: וַיִּקְח֣וּ אֶֽת־יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ וַיַּשְׁלִ֨כוּ אֹת֜וֹ אֶל־הַבּ֣וֹר׀מַלְכִּיָּ֣הוּ בֶן־הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֲשֶׁר֙ בַּחֲצַ֣ר הַמַּטָּרָ֔ה וַיְשַׁלְּח֥וּ אֶֽת־יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ בַּחֲבָלִ֑ים וּבַבּ֤וֹר אֵֽין־מַ֨יִם֙ כִּ֣י אִם־טִ֔יט וַיִּטְבַּ֥ע יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ בַּטִּֽיט׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they took Jeremiah and threw him into the cistern of Malchiah son of the king, which [was] in [the] courtyard of the guard; and they let down Jeremiah with the ropes; and in the cistern there was not water but mud, and sank Jeremiah in the mud.

en.L: So they took Jeremiah and threw him into the cistern of Malchiah the son of the king, which [was] in the courtyard of the guard, and they let Jeremiah down with ropes. And in the cistern there was no water, only mud, and Jeremiah sank in the mud.
en.B: So they took Jeremiah and threw him into the cistern of Malchiah, the king's son, in the courtyard of the guard. They let him down with ropes. There was no water in the cistern, only mud, and Jeremiah sank down into the mud.
en.R: So they took Jeremiah and threw him into the cistern of Malchiah, the king's son. It was in the courtyard of the guard. They lowered Jeremiah into it with ropes. There was no water in the cistern, only mud, and Jeremiah sank down in it.

decisions.choice: cistern: a pit cut into the rock to store rainwater
decisions.reason: Cisterns were dug out of the rock, narrow at the top and wide below, to hold the winter rain. In the long siege this one had no water left, only mud at the bottom. The same word can mean a pit or a dungeon (37:16).

decisions.choice: the king's son: a prince, or a royal officer
decisions.reason: "The king's son" may mean a son of the royal family, or it may be the title of an officer of the king (36:26). Either way the cistern belonged to someone close to the king.

decisions.choice: the courtyard of the guard: an enclosed court of the palace
decisions.reason: This was the court where prisoners were kept under the watch of the royal guard (32:2; 37:21). Jeremiah was already held there, so the officials did not have to take him far.

decisions.choice: threw him ... let him down with ropes: one act told twice
decisions.reason: They cast Jeremiah into the cistern, and the next clause says how: by lowering him on ropes. The second statement explains the first.

decisions.choice: cistern
decisions.reason: "Cistern" says what the pit was made for, which matters because it had no water (m1).

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֡ע עֶֽבֶד־מֶ֨לֶךְ הַכּוּשִׁ֜י אִ֣ישׁ סָרִ֗יס וְהוּא֙ בְּבֵ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּֽי־נָתְנ֥וּ אֶֽת־יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ אֶל־הַבּ֑וֹר וְהַמֶּ֥לֶךְ יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּשַׁ֥עַר בִּנְיָמִֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard Ebed-melech the Cushite, a man, a eunuch, and he [was] in [the] house of the king, that they had put Jeremiah into the cistern; and the king [was] sitting in [the] gate of Benjamin.

en.L: And Ebed-melech the Cushite, a eunuch, who [was] in the house of the king, heard that they had put Jeremiah into the cistern. And the king [was] sitting in the Gate of Benjamin.
en.B: Ebed-melech the Cushite, a court officer in the king's palace, heard that they had put Jeremiah into the cistern. At the time the king was sitting at the Benjamin Gate.
en.R: Ebed-melech was a palace official from Cush who served the king. He heard that Jeremiah had been put into the cistern. At that time the king was sitting at the Benjamin Gate.

decisions.choice: Ebed-melech: a name meaning "servant of the king"
decisions.reason: The name means "servant of the king". It may have been a court name or title given to a foreign servant rather than the name he was born with. The king's own servant does what the king's officials would not.

decisions.choice: the Cushite: a man from Cush
decisions.reason: Cush was the land south of Egypt along the upper Nile, in what is now Sudan (13:23). Men from Cush served in the courts of the region (2 Samuel 18:21).

decisions.choice: eunuch: a castrated man serving at court, or a court official
decisions.reason: The word names men who were made eunuchs to serve at a royal court, especially among the women of the palace. It is also used more loosely of a high official: Potiphar, who had a wife, is called by it (Genesis 39:1). Here it may mean either.

decisions.choice: the king was sitting in the Benjamin Gate: in public, at a city gate
decisions.reason: Kings and elders sat in the gates to hear cases and do public business (2 Samuel 19:9; Ruth 4:1). The Benjamin Gate was on the north side, facing the land of Benjamin (37:13). Ebed-melech went to the king there, in the open.

decisions.choice: eunuch (L); court officer (B); palace official (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this word in Jeremiah, as in 2 Kings 24:12: Literal "eunuch", Balanced "court officer", Readable "palace official"; "official" alone is kept for the word for a leader (sar). The note (m3) gives the full sense.

decisions.choice: Ebed-melech was a palace official from Cush ... He heard
decisions.reason: Readable first says who Ebed-melech was, then what he heard, and says "from Cush" for "the Cushite".

source.text: וַיֵּצֵ֥א עֶֽבֶד־מֶ֖לֶךְ מִבֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אֶל־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out Ebed-melech from [the] house of the king and spoke to the king, saying,

en.L: And Ebed-melech went out from the house of the king and spoke to the king, saying,
en.B: So Ebed-melech went out of the palace and spoke to the king:
en.R: So Ebed-melech left the palace and went to speak to the king. He said,

decisions.choice: went out from the palace: to the gate where the king was
decisions.reason: The king was not in the palace but sitting at the Benjamin Gate (verse 7), so Ebed-melech went out to find him there.

decisions.choice: spoke to the king: a servant speaking up before the king in public
decisions.reason: A palace servant from abroad accuses the king's own officials before him. His courage stands against the king's weakness in verse 5.

decisions.choice: went to speak
decisions.reason: Readable says that he went to where the king was (m1).

source.text: אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ הֵרֵ֜עוּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ אֵ֣ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשׂוּ֙ לְיִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֔יא אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־הִשְׁלִ֖יכוּ אֶל־הַבּ֑וֹר וַיָּ֤מָת תַּחְתָּיו֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י הָֽרָעָ֔ב כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין הַלֶּ֛חֶם ע֖וֹד בָּעִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: My lord the king, have done evil the men these [in] all that they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, whom they have thrown into the cistern; and he will die in his place because of the famine, for there is no the bread any more in the city.

en.L: "My lord the king, these men have done evil in all that they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, whom they have thrown into the cistern; and he will die where he is because of the famine, for there is no more bread in the city."
en.B: "My lord the king, these men have acted wickedly in everything they have done to Jeremiah the prophet. They have thrown him into the cistern, and he will die there of hunger, for there is no bread left in the city."
en.R: "My lord the king, these men have done a very evil thing to Jeremiah the prophet. They have thrown him into the cistern! He will starve to death down there, because there is no bread left anywhere in the city."

decisions.choice: and he will die: as good as dead
decisions.reason: The form of the verb usually tells what happened next in a story, "and he died". Here it states what will surely follow: left in the cistern, he is as good as dead.

decisions.choice: in his place: where he is
decisions.reason: "Under him" or "in his place" means on the spot, down there in the cistern.

decisions.choice: no bread left in the city: the end of the siege was near
decisions.reason: The king had ordered that Jeremiah be given a loaf a day "until all the bread in the city was gone" (37:21). That time had come (52:6). No one would feed a man in a cistern.

decisions.choice: have done evil: have acted wrongly
decisions.reason: The verb means to do harm or to act wickedly. Ebed-melech calls the officials' deed plainly wrong, before the king who allowed it.

decisions.choice: starve to death down there
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what dying "because of the famine" in the cistern would mean.

decisions.choice: have done a very evil thing to
decisions.reason: Readable puts "have done evil in all that they have done" in one plain clause.

source.text: וַיְצַוֶּ֣ה הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֵ֛ת עֶֽבֶד־מֶ֥לֶךְ הַכּוּשִׁ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר קַ֣ח בְּיָדְךָ֤ מִזֶּה֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְֽהַעֲלִ֜יתָ אֶֽת־יִרְמְיָ֧הוּ הַנָּבִ֛יא מִן־הַבּ֖וֹר בְּטֶ֥רֶם יָמֽוּת׃

records.literal_gloss: And commanded the king Ebed-melech the Cushite, saying, Take under your hand from here thirty men, and bring up Jeremiah the prophet from the cistern before he dies.

en.L: And the king commanded Ebed-melech the Cushite, saying, "Take under your hand thirty men from here, and bring up Jeremiah the prophet from the cistern before he dies."
en.B: Then the king gave Ebed-melech the Cushite this order: "Take thirty men with you from here, and pull Jeremiah the prophet up from the cistern before he dies."
en.R: So the king gave an order to Ebed-melech from Cush. "Take thirty men from here with you," he said. "Lift Jeremiah the prophet out of the cistern before he dies."

decisions.choice: thirty men: the Hebrew text as handed down
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text and the early translations read "thirty". One Hebrew manuscript reads "three", and it has been suggested that "three" was the first reading, since a few men are enough to pull one man up by ropes. A larger band may have been needed to protect the rescue from the officials.

decisions.choice: take under your hand: take under your command
decisions.reason: Men "under your hand" are men placed at your orders (verse 11).

decisions.choice: the king commanded: Zedekiah undoes what he allowed in verse 5
decisions.reason: The king who said he could do nothing against his officials now gives an order against what they have done.

decisions.choice: with you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "under your hand" (m2).

decisions.choice: from Cush
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח׀עֶֽבֶד־מֶ֨לֶךְ אֶת־הָאֲנָשִׁ֜ים בְּיָד֗וֹ וַיָּבֹ֤א בֵית־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶל־תַּ֣חַת הָאוֹצָ֔ר וַיִּקַּ֤ח מִשָּׁם֙ בְּלוֹיֵ֣ סְחָב֔וֹת וּבְלוֹיֵ֖ מְלָחִ֑ים וַיְשַׁלְּחֵ֧ם אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֛הוּ אֶל־הַבּ֖וֹר בַּחֲבָלִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And took Ebed-melech the men under his hand and went [to the] house of the king, to under the storehouse, and took from there worn-out [pieces of] rags and worn-out [pieces of] clothes, and let them down to Jeremiah into the cistern with the ropes.

en.L: And Ebed-melech took the men under his hand and went into the house of the king, to [a place] under the storehouse, and took from there worn-out rags and worn-out clothes, and let them down to Jeremiah in the cistern with ropes.
en.B: So Ebed-melech went into the palace with the men, to a room beneath the storehouse. He took some old rags and worn-out clothes from there and let them down on ropes to Jeremiah in the cistern.
en.R: So Ebed-melech took the men with him and went to a room under the storehouse in the palace. He got some old rags and worn-out clothes there. Then he lowered them on ropes to Jeremiah in the cistern.

decisions.choice: under the storehouse: a room below the palace storehouse
alternatives: to the wardrobe of the storehouse
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "to under the storehouse", a place below the room where the palace kept its goods. A small change to the Hebrew would give "to the wardrobe of the storehouse", where clothes were kept; the sense of where he found the rags is much the same either way.

decisions.choice: worn-out rags and worn-out clothes: old cloth no one needed
decisions.reason: Both words for the cloth mean things torn or worn out, and both are called "worn-out". They were scraps fit for nothing, which became the means of the rescue.

decisions.choice: rags: the written form and the form read aloud differ slightly
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew and the margin differ slightly in how this word is written. The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: [a place] under (L); a room beneath / under (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "to under the storehouse". Literal brackets the word it needs; Balanced and Readable say "room".

decisions.choice: with him
decisions.reason: As in verse 10.

source.text: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר עֶבֶד־מֶ֨לֶךְ הַכּוּשִׁ֜י אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ שִׂ֣ים נָ֠א בְּלוֹאֵ֨י הַסְּחָב֤וֹת וְהַמְּלָחִים֙ תַּ֚חַת אַצִּל֣וֹת יָדֶ֔יךָ מִתַּ֖חַת לַחֲבָלִ֑ים וַיַּ֥עַשׂ יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ כֵּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Ebed-melech the Cushite to Jeremiah, Put please the worn-out [pieces of] the rags and the clothes under [the] joints of your hands, under the ropes. And did Jeremiah so.

en.L: And Ebed-melech the Cushite said to Jeremiah, "Put, please, the worn-out rags and clothes under the joints of your arms, under the ropes." And Jeremiah did so.
en.B: Ebed-melech the Cushite said to Jeremiah, "Put these old rags and worn-out clothes under your armpits, between you and the ropes." Jeremiah did so.
en.R: Ebed-melech from Cush called down to Jeremiah, "Put these old rags and clothes under your arms, so the ropes will not hurt you." Jeremiah did what he said.

decisions.choice: the joints of your hands: your armpits
decisions.reason: The "joints" of the arms are where the arms meet the body. The ropes were to go under his arms.

decisions.choice: under the ropes: padding between the ropes and his body
decisions.reason: A man stuck in deep mud and weak with hunger would be cut by bare ropes as he was pulled up. The rags took the strain.

decisions.choice: please: a kind and polite request
decisions.reason: Ebed-melech speaks to the prophet with a polite word, "please". The kindness of the act runs through his words.

decisions.choice: between you and the ropes
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "under the ropes" means here (m2).

decisions.choice: called down ... so the ropes will not hurt you
decisions.reason: Readable says that he spoke from above the cistern and what the rags were for (m2).

decisions.choice: please left unexpressed
decisions.reason: The polite word is carried by the friendly tone of the request in Balanced and Readable; Literal keeps it.

source.text: וַיִּמְשְׁכ֤וּ אֶֽת־יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ בַּֽחֲבָלִ֔ים וַיַּעֲל֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ מִן־הַבּ֑וֹר וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ בַּחֲצַ֖ר הַמַּטָּרָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they drew Jeremiah with the ropes and brought him up from the cistern; and remained Jeremiah in [the] courtyard of the guard.

en.L: And they drew Jeremiah up with the ropes and brought him up out of the cistern. And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard.
en.B: Then they drew Jeremiah up by the ropes and brought him out of the cistern, and Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard.
en.R: Then they pulled Jeremiah up with the ropes and got him out of the cistern. After that, Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard.

decisions.choice: remained in the courtyard of the guard: rescued, but still a prisoner
decisions.reason: Jeremiah is saved from the cistern but goes back to the custody he was in before (37:21). The line returns at the end of the chapter (verse 28).

decisions.choice: the rescue and its reward
decisions.reason: Later the LORD sends Ebed-melech a promise that he will be kept safe when the city falls, because he trusted the LORD (39:15-18).

decisions.choice: After that
decisions.reason: Readable marks that this is what followed the rescue.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֞ח הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֗הוּ וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶֽת־יִרְמְיָ֤הוּ הַנָּבִיא֙ אֵלָ֔יו אֶל־מָבוֹא֙ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ שֹׁאֵ֨ל אֲנִ֤י אֹֽתְךָ֙ דָּבָ֔ר אַל־תְּכַחֵ֥ד מִמֶּ֖נִּי דָּבָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent the king Zedekiah and took Jeremiah the prophet to him to [the] entrance the third which [was] in [the] house of Yahweh; and said the king to Jeremiah, Asking I [am] you a thing; do not hide from me a thing.

en.L: And King Zedekiah sent and took Jeremiah the prophet to himself at the third entrance that [is] in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And the king said to Jeremiah, "I am going to ask you something; do not hide anything from me."
en.B: King Zedekiah sent for Jeremiah the prophet and had him brought to him at the third entrance of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The king said to Jeremiah, "I am going to ask you something. Do not hide anything from me."
en.R: Then King Zedekiah sent for Jeremiah the prophet. He had him brought to the third entrance of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple. The king said to Jeremiah, "I want to ask you something. Do not hide anything from me."

decisions.choice: the third entrance: a gateway of the temple not named elsewhere
decisions.reason: This entrance is not mentioned anywhere else, and its place is not known. It may have been a private way from the palace into the temple area (compare the king's entrance in 2 Kings 16:18), where the king could meet Jeremiah unseen.

decisions.choice: a thing: a matter, or a word
decisions.reason: The same word means "thing" and "word". The king asks "a word" of Jeremiah and wants no "word" held back, much as he asked in secret before, "Is there a word from the LORD?" (37:17).

decisions.choice: sent and took: the king had Jeremiah brought from the courtyard of the guard
decisions.reason: As in 37:17, Zedekiah does not go to the prophet but has him fetched, and the meeting is kept secret (verses 16, 24-27).

decisions.choice: sent for ... had him brought
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "sent and took" means.

decisions.choice: temple
decisions.reason: Readable says "temple" for "the house of the LORD", as elsewhere in Jeremiah.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ אֶל־צִדְקִיָּ֔הוּ כִּ֚י אַגִּ֣יד לְךָ֔ הֲל֖וֹא הָמֵ֣ת תְּמִיתֵ֑נִי וְכִי֙ אִיעָ֣צְךָ֔ לֹ֥א תִשְׁמַ֖ע אֵלָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Jeremiah to Zedekiah, If I tell you, [will] not surely you put me to death? And if I counsel you, not you will listen to me.

en.L: And Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "If I tell you, will you not surely put me to death? And if I give you counsel, you will not listen to me."
en.B: Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "If I tell you, will you not certainly have me put to death? And if I give you advice, you will not listen to me."
en.R: Jeremiah answered Zedekiah, "If I tell you the truth, you will surely have me killed! And if I give you advice, you will not take it."

decisions.choice: will you not surely put me to death: a question that expects the answer yes
decisions.reason: The question is not a request for information. Jeremiah means that the truth will cost him his life. The doubled verb, "putting to death you will put me to death", makes it stronger.

decisions.choice: you will not listen to me: as the king never has
decisions.reason: Jeremiah knows the king's pattern: he asks for the LORD's word but does not obey it (37:2, 17).

decisions.choice: you will surely have me killed! (R)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it means (m1).

decisions.choice: you will not take it
decisions.reason: Readable says "not take" advice for "not listen to" it; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: the truth
decisions.reason: Readable says what Jeremiah would tell the king: the LORD's true word, as verses 17-23 give it.

source.text: וַיִּשָּׁבַ֞ע הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֛הוּ אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ בַּסֵּ֣תֶר לֵאמֹ֑ר חַי־יְהוָ֞ה אֲשֶׁר֩ עָשָׂה־לָ֨נוּ אֶת־הַנֶּ֤פֶשׁ הַזֹּאת֙ אִם־אֲמִיתֶ֔ךָ וְאִם־אֶתֶּנְךָ֗ בְּיַד֙ הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֥ר מְבַקְשִׁ֖ים אֶת־נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And swore the king Zedekiah to Jeremiah in secret, saying, [As] lives Yahweh, who made for us the life this, if I put you to death, and if I give you into [the] hand of the men these who [are] seeking your life.

en.L: And King Zedekiah swore to Jeremiah in secret, saying, "As {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, who made this life for us, I will not put you to death, and I will not give you into the hand of these men who are seeking your life."
en.B: But King Zedekiah swore an oath to Jeremiah in secret: "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, who gave us this life, I will not put you to death, and I will not hand you over to these men who want to kill you."
en.R: So King Zedekiah made a secret promise to Jeremiah. "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, the one who gave us life," he said, "I will not have you killed. And I will not hand you over to these men who want to kill you."

decisions.choice: if I put you to death ... if I give you: a promise made under oath, "I will not"
decisions.reason: In a Hebrew oath, "if I do this" leaves unsaid "may God punish me", so it means "I will surely not do this" (1 Samuel 24:7).

decisions.choice: this life: the life and breath God gives
decisions.reason: The word means life, breath, the living self. Zedekiah swears by the LORD who gives life, as he promises to spare a life that the officials are trying to take.

decisions.choice: seeking your life: trying to kill you
decisions.reason: To seek someone's life is to want them dead (11:21; 19:7).

decisions.choice: who made: a small word written in the text but not read aloud
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has a small word before "who" that the margin tells readers to leave out. It does not change the sense.

decisions.choice: As surely as the LORD lives
decisions.reason: The usual wording for this oath at Balanced and Readable; Literal keeps the short Hebrew form.

decisions.choice: made a secret promise
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that he swore an oath without being seen.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֣הוּ אֶל־צִדְקִיָּ֡הוּ כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֩ אֱלֹהֵ֨י צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אִם־יָצֹ֨א תֵצֵ֜א אֶל־שָׂרֵ֤י מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶל֙ וְחָיְתָ֣ה נַפְשֶׁ֔ךָ וְהָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את לֹ֥א תִשָּׂרֵ֖ף בָּאֵ֑שׁ וְחָיִ֖תָה אַתָּ֥ה וּבֵיתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Jeremiah to Zedekiah, Thus says Yahweh, God of hosts, God of Israel: If surely you go out to [the] princes of [the] king of Babylon, then will live your soul, and the city this not will be burned with the fire; and you will live, you and your house.

en.L: And Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of hosts, the God of Israel: 'If you will indeed go out to the commanders of the king of Babylon, then your soul will live, and this city will not be burned with fire; and you will live, you and your house.
en.B: Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: 'If you will surrender to the commanders of the king of Babylon, your life will be spared, and this city will not be burned down. You and your family will live.
en.R: Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: 'You must surrender to the commanders of the king of Babylon. If you do, you will stay alive, and this city will not be burned down. You and your family will live.

decisions.choice: go out to: surrender to
decisions.reason: To go out of a besieged city to the enemy's commanders is to give oneself up (verse 2; 2 Kings 24:12). The verb is doubled, "if going out you go out", to press the choice on the king.

decisions.choice: your soul will live: you yourself will live
decisions.reason: The word often rendered "soul" means the living person, the self or life. To say "your soul will live" is to say that the king's own life will be spared.

decisions.choice: your house: your household, your family
decisions.reason: "House" here means the king's family and household (verse 23), not a building.

decisions.choice: the God of hosts
decisions.reason: The title names God as lord of the armies of heaven and earth; the note at Isaiah 1:9 explains it.

decisions.choice: commanders (all levels)
decisions.reason: The same word as for Judah's officials in verses 4, 25 and 27, but here it names the officers of the army besieging the city (39:3, 13), so it takes the wording set for the word in a military setting.

decisions.choice: You must surrender ... If you do
decisions.reason: Readable puts the condition as a command followed by its result, which says the same thing in shorter sentences.

decisions.choice: your life will be spared (B); you will stay alive (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "your soul will live" (m2).

source.text: וְאִ֣ם לֹֽא־תֵצֵ֗א אֶל־שָׂרֵי֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל וְנִתְּנָ֞ה הָעִ֤יר הַזֹּאת֙ בְּיַ֣ד הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים וּשְׂרָפ֖וּהָ בָּאֵ֑שׁ וְאַתָּ֖ה לֹֽא־תִמָּלֵ֥ט מִיָּדָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: But if not you go out to [the] princes of [the] king of Babylon, then will be given the city this into [the] hand of the Chaldeans, and they will burn it with the fire, and you not you will escape from their hand.

en.L: But if you do not go out to the commanders of the king of Babylon, then this city will be given into the hand of the Chaldeans, and they will burn it with fire, and you yourself will not escape from their hand.'"
en.B: But if you do not surrender to the commanders of the king of Babylon, this city will be handed over to the Chaldeans, and they will burn it down. And you yourself will not escape from them.'"
en.R: But if you do not surrender to the commanders of the king of Babylon, this city will be handed over to the Babylonians. They will burn it to the ground, and you will not escape from them.'"

decisions.choice: and you: the king himself, set apart from the city
decisions.reason: "You" is written out for emphasis. The city will burn, and the king will not get away either (21:7; 32:4; 34:3).

decisions.choice: into the hand of ... from their hand: into their power ... from their power
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power, as in verse 3.

decisions.choice: surrender
decisions.reason: As in verse 17.

decisions.choice: commanders (all levels)
decisions.reason: The same word as for Judah's officials in verses 4, 25 and 27, but here it names the officers of the army besieging the city (39:3, 13), so it takes the wording set for the word in a military setting.

decisions.choice: Babylonians
decisions.reason: The wording set for the Chaldeans at Readable.

source.text: וַיֹּ֛אמֶר הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֑הוּ אֲנִ֧י דֹאֵ֣ג אֶת־הַיְּהוּדִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָֽפְלוּ֙ אֶל־הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים פֶּֽן־יִתְּנ֥וּ אֹתִ֛י בְּיָדָ֖ם וְהִתְעַלְּלוּ־בִֽי׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And said the king Zedekiah to Jeremiah, I [am] afraid of the Judeans who have fallen to the Chaldeans, lest they give me into their hand and they deal abusively with me.

en.L: And King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "I am afraid of the Judeans who have fallen away to the Chaldeans, lest they give me into their hand and they deal abusively with me."
en.B: King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "I am afraid of the Judeans who have deserted to the Chaldeans. They may hand me over to them, and they will treat me cruelly."
en.R: King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "I am afraid of the people of Judah who have already gone over to the Babylonians. The Babylonians might hand me over to them, and they would make fun of me and treat me cruelly."

decisions.choice: fallen to the Chaldeans: deserted to the enemy
decisions.reason: To fall to an army is to desert and give oneself up to it (21:9; 37:13-14). Many in the city had done what Jeremiah urged (39:9; 52:15).

decisions.choice: lest they give me into their hand: the Chaldeans might hand the king over to the deserters
decisions.reason: "They give" means the Chaldeans, and "their hand" the Judeans who had deserted. The king fears the very people who once followed him.

decisions.choice: deal abusively with me: mock and mistreat me
decisions.reason: The verb is used of making sport of someone, toying with a helpless enemy and shaming him (Exodus 10:2; Judges 19:25; 1 Samuel 31:4).

decisions.choice: The Babylonians might hand me over
decisions.reason: Readable names who would hand the king over (m2). Balanced keeps "They" as the Hebrew does, which the sentence before makes clear.

decisions.choice: the people of Judah
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who the Judeans were.

decisions.choice: make fun of me and treat me cruelly
decisions.reason: Readable uses two plain verbs for the two sides of the Hebrew word, mockery and cruelty (m3).

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ לֹ֣א יִתֵּ֑נוּ שְֽׁמַֽע־נָ֣א׀בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֗ה לַאֲשֶׁ֤ר אֲנִי֙ דֹּבֵ֣ר אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְיִ֥יטַב לְךָ֖ וּתְחִ֥י נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Jeremiah, Not they will give [you]. Listen please to [the] voice of Yahweh in what I [am] speaking to you, and it will go well for you, and will live your soul.

en.L: And Jeremiah said, "They will not give [you over]. Listen, please, to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in what I am speaking to you, and it will go well with you, and your soul will live.
en.B: Jeremiah said, "They will not hand you over. Please obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s voice in what I am telling you. Then it will go well with you, and your life will be spared.
en.R: Jeremiah answered, "They will not hand you over to them. Please do what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says, as I am telling you. Then things will go well for you, and you will stay alive.

decisions.choice: listen to the voice of the LORD: obey the LORD
decisions.reason: To listen to someone's voice is to do what they say (26:13).

decisions.choice: they will not give you over: an answer to the king's fear
decisions.reason: Jeremiah takes up the king's own words from verse 19, "lest they give me", and answers them: the Chaldeans will not hand him over to the deserters.

decisions.choice: your soul will live: you yourself will live
decisions.reason: As in verse 17.

decisions.choice: obey (B); do what the LORD says (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m1).

decisions.choice: your life will be spared (B); you will stay alive (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 17.

source.text: וְאִם־מָאֵ֥ן אַתָּ֖ה לָצֵ֑את זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִרְאַ֖נִי יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: But if refusing you [are] to go out, this [is] the word that has shown me Yahweh:

en.L: But if you refuse to go out, this [is] the word that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has shown me:
en.B: But if you refuse to surrender, this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has shown me:
en.R: But if you refuse to surrender, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has shown me what will happen.

decisions.choice: has shown me: has let me see in a vision
decisions.reason: The verb means "cause to see". What Jeremiah saw follows in verse 22, as if it were already happening (compare 24:1).

decisions.choice: the word: the thing, the matter
decisions.reason: The same Hebrew word means "word" and "thing". Here it is what the LORD has made known: the scene that follows.

decisions.choice: surrender
decisions.reason: As in verse 17.

decisions.choice: what will happen
decisions.reason: Readable says what the "word" here is (m2).

source.text: וְהִנֵּ֣ה כָל־הַנָּשִׁ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר נִשְׁאֲרוּ֙ בְּבֵ֣ית מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֔ה מוּצָא֕וֹת אֶל־שָׂרֵ֖י מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֑ל וְהֵ֣נָּה אֹמְר֗וֹת הִסִּית֜וּךָ וְיָכְל֤וּ לְךָ֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י שְׁלֹמֶ֔ךָ הָטְבְּע֥וּ בַבֹּ֛ץ רַגְלֶ֖ךָ נָסֹ֥גוּ אָחֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: And look, all the women who are left in [the] house of [the] king of Judah [are] being brought out to [the] princes of [the] king of Babylon, and they [are] saying, They have misled you and they have prevailed over you, [the] men of your peace; they have been sunk in the mire your feet, they have turned back.

en.L: And look, all the women who are left in the house of the king of Judah [are] being brought out to the commanders of the king of Babylon, \q and they are saying, 'They have misled you and prevailed over you, \q the men of your peace; \q your feet are sunk in the mire, \q they have turned back.'
en.B: Look, all the women who are left in the palace of the king of Judah are being led out to the commanders of the king of Babylon, \q and they are saying, 'Your trusted friends \q have misled you and overpowered you; \q now your feet are sunk in the mud, \q they have turned their backs on you.'
en.R: I saw all the women who are left in the palace of the king of Judah being led out to the commanders of the king of Babylon. \q They were saying to you, 'Your closest friends fooled you; \q they got the better of you. \q Now your feet are stuck in the mud, \q and they have left you there.'

decisions.choice: the men of your peace: your trusted friends and allies
decisions.reason: "The men of your peace" are those one is at peace with, friends one trusts (20:10; Psalm 41:10; Obadiah 7). Here they are the officials and prophets who urged the king to hold out.

decisions.choice: the women of the palace brought out: the king's household taken by the conqueror
decisions.reason: The women of a king's household were handed over to the one who defeated him, a sign that his rule was ended (2 Samuel 16:21-22; 1 Kings 2:22).

decisions.choice: they are saying: the women sing a short lament over the king
decisions.reason: Their words fall into the short, uneven lines of a lament, sung here in mockery over the king who trusted the wrong friends.

decisions.choice: your feet are sunk in the mud: you are stuck and helpless
decisions.reason: Feet stuck in mud cannot move (Psalm 69:3, 15). The king who let Jeremiah sink in the mud of the cistern (verse 6) will himself be stuck, with no one to pull him out. The word for mud is not the same as in verse 6, but the picture is.

decisions.choice: they have turned back: they have deserted you
decisions.reason: To turn back is to retreat or turn away (46:5). The friends who misled the king leave him when he is stuck.

decisions.choice: I saw
decisions.reason: Readable says that "look" introduces what the LORD showed Jeremiah (verse 21). The women and their words are seen as if it were happening now.

decisions.choice: Your trusted friends (B); Your closest friends (R) first
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the friends after the verbs; Balanced and Readable name them first so the sentence is clear.

decisions.choice: now
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "now" to show that the stuck feet come after the friends' bad advice; the Hebrew sets the lines side by side.

source.text: וְאֶת־כָּל־נָשֶׁ֣יךָ וְאֶת־בָּנֶ֗יךָ מֽוֹצִאִים֙ אֶל־הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים וְאַתָּ֖ה לֹא־תִמָּלֵ֣ט מִיָּדָ֑ם כִּ֣י בְיַ֤ד מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶל֙ תִּתָּפֵ֔שׂ וְאֶת־הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את תִּשְׂרֹ֥ף בָּאֵֽשׁ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And all your wives and your children [they are] bringing out to the Chaldeans, and you, not you will escape from their hand, for by [the] hand of [the] king of Babylon you will be seized, and the city this you will burn with the fire.

en.L: And all your wives and your children they will bring out to the Chaldeans, and you yourself will not escape from their hand, for you will be seized by the hand of the king of Babylon, and this city you will burn with fire."
en.B: All your wives and your children will be led out to the Chaldeans, and you yourself will not escape from them. You will be captured by the king of Babylon, and you will be the cause of this city being burned down."
en.R: All your wives and children will be taken out to the Babylonians. You yourself will not escape from them. The king of Babylon will capture you. And it will be your fault that this city is burned to the ground."

decisions.choice: you will burn this city: you will bring about its burning
alternatives: this city will be burned with fire
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "this city you will burn": the king's refusal will be the cause of the fire. By a change of one vowel the same letters read "this city will be burned", which the Greek translation and some Hebrew manuscripts have. Either way the city burns because the king will not surrender.

decisions.choice: they are bringing out: people will lead them out
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject; it means that the king's family will be led out to the enemy. Jeremiah speaks of it as already under way.

decisions.choice: you will be seized: what happened when the city fell
decisions.reason: Zedekiah was caught as he fled, his sons were killed before his eyes, and the city was burned (39:4-8; 52:8-13).

decisions.choice: you will be the cause of this city being burned down (B); it will be your fault that this city is burned (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "you will burn this city" means here (m1).

decisions.choice: will be led out (B); will be taken out (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the passive for the verb with no subject (m2).

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר צִדְקִיָּ֜הוּ אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ אִ֛ישׁ אַל־יֵדַ֥ע בַּדְּבָֽרִים־הָאֵ֖לֶּה וְלֹ֥א תָמֽוּת׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Zedekiah to Jeremiah, Anyone not let know of the words these, and not you will die.

en.L: And Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "Let no one know of these words, and you will not die.
en.B: Then Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "Do not let anyone know about this conversation, and you will not die.
en.R: Then Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "Do not let anyone know what we talked about. If you keep it secret, you will not die.

decisions.choice: and you will not die: a promise that is also a warning
decisions.reason: If no one learns of the meeting, Jeremiah will be safe. The words also hint that he will be in danger, from the officials or the king, if he speaks.

decisions.choice: these words: this conversation
decisions.reason: "Words" here means all that the two men said to each other.

decisions.choice: If you keep it secret
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the condition the Hebrew joins with "and" (m1).

decisions.choice: this conversation
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of "these words" (m2).

source.text: וְכִֽי־יִשְׁמְע֣וּ הַשָּׂרִים֮ כִּֽי־דִבַּ֣רְתִּי אִתָּךְ֒ וּבָ֣אוּ אֵלֶ֣יךָ וְֽאָמְר֪וּ אֵלֶ֟יךָ הַגִּֽידָה־נָּ֨א לָ֜נוּ מַה־דִּבַּ֧רְתָּ אֶל־הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אַל־תְּכַחֵ֥ד מִמֶּ֖נּוּ וְלֹ֣א נְמִיתֶ֑ךָ וּמַה־דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יךָ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And if hear the princes that I have spoken with you, and they come to you and say to you, Tell please to us what you said to the king, do not hide [it] from us, and not we will put you to death, and what said to you the king,

en.L: And if the princes hear that I have spoken with you, and they come to you and say to you, 'Tell us, please, what you said to the king; do not hide [it] from us, and we will not put you to death; and what did the king say to you?'
en.B: If the officials hear that I have talked with you, and they come and say to you, 'Tell us what you said to the king and what the king said to you. Do not hide anything from us, and we will not put you to death,'
en.R: The leaders may hear that I have talked with you. They may come to you and say, 'Tell us what you said to the king and what the king said to you. Do not hide anything from us, and we will not kill you.'

decisions.choice: if the officials hear ...: the sentence goes on into verse 26
decisions.reason: Verse 25 sets out what may happen, and verse 26 tells Jeremiah what to say if it does.

decisions.choice: and we will not put you to death: their promise if he tells them
decisions.reason: The officials offer to spare him if he holds nothing back, which shows what they would do if he did.

decisions.choice: and what did the king say to you: the second half of their question, put last
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets the officials' promise between the two parts of their question, as people do when they speak in haste.

decisions.choice: princes (L); officials (B); leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this word in Jeremiah (1:18). These are the king's chief officers, not his sons.

decisions.choice: what you said to the king and what the king said to you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring the two parts of the question together (m3).

decisions.choice: The leaders may hear ... They may come
decisions.reason: Readable turns the long condition into short sentences of its own.

source.text: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם מַפִּיל־אֲנִ֥י תְחִנָּתִ֖י לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ לְבִלְתִּ֧י הֲשִׁיבֵ֛נִי בֵּ֥ית יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן לָמ֥וּת שָֽׁם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: then you will say to them, Making fall I [was] my plea before the king, not to send me back [to the] house of Jonathan to die there.

en.L: then you will say to them, 'I was presenting my plea before the king, that he not send me back to the house of Jonathan to die there.'"
en.B: then say to them, 'I was presenting my plea to the king not to send me back to the house of Jonathan to die there.'"
en.R: If that happens, tell them, 'I was begging the king not to send me back to Jonathan's house to die there.'"

decisions.choice: presenting my plea: laying a humble request before the king
decisions.reason: Literally "making my plea fall" before the king, the picture of a request laid down at a superior's feet (36:7; 37:20).

decisions.choice: the house of Jonathan: the prison of 37:15
decisions.reason: Jeremiah had been held in the house of Jonathan the secretary, which had been made a prison, and had begged the king not to send him back there (37:15-16, 20).

decisions.choice: what Jeremiah is to say: a true plea, but not the whole conversation
decisions.reason: Jeremiah had made this very plea in 37:20. The king tells him to give that answer and not the rest; the text records it without praise or blame.

decisions.choice: If that happens
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence and links it back to verse 25.

decisions.choice: begging
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "presenting my plea" (m1).

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ כָל־הַשָּׂרִ֤ים אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ וַיִּשְׁאֲל֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ וַיַּגֵּ֤ד לָהֶם֙ כְּכָל־הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּ֖ה הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיַּחֲרִ֣שׁוּ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ כִּ֥י לֹֽא־נִשְׁמַ֖ע הַדָּבָֽר׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And came all the princes to Jeremiah and asked him, and he told them according to all the words these that had commanded the king; and they were silent from him, for not had been heard the matter.

en.L: And all the princes came to Jeremiah and asked him, and he told them according to all these words that the king had commanded. And they kept silent from him, for the matter had not been heard.
en.B: All the officials came to Jeremiah and questioned him, and he answered them with the very words the king had told him to say. So they stopped questioning him, for no one had overheard the conversation.
en.R: All the leaders came to Jeremiah and questioned him. He told them just what the king had told him to say. So they left him alone, because no one had heard what the king and Jeremiah said to each other.

decisions.choice: they kept silent from him: they stopped questioning him
decisions.reason: To fall silent from someone is to leave off speaking with him (1 Samuel 7:8). The officials had nothing more to ask.

decisions.choice: the matter had not been heard: no one had overheard the talk
decisions.reason: The meeting had been secret (verse 16), so the officials could not show that anything else had been said.

decisions.choice: princes (L); officials (B); leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this word in Jeremiah (1:18). These are the king's chief officers, not his sons.

decisions.choice: stopped questioning him (B); left him alone (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m1).

source.text: וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ בַּחֲצַ֣ר הַמַּטָּרָ֔ה עַד־י֖וֹם אֲשֶׁר־נִלְכְּדָ֣ה יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑םסוְהָיָ֕ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר נִלְכְּדָ֖ה יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And remained Jeremiah in [the] courtyard of the guard until [the] day that was captured Jerusalem. And it was, when was captured Jerusalem,

en.L: And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard until the day that Jerusalem was captured. And it happened, when Jerusalem was captured,
en.B: So Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard until the day Jerusalem fell. This is what happened when Jerusalem was captured:
en.R: Jeremiah was kept in the courtyard of the guard until the day Jerusalem fell. This is what happened when Jerusalem was captured.

decisions.choice: and it happened, when Jerusalem was captured: the opening of the account in chapter 39
decisions.reason: The last words of the verse begin the next part of the story. After a note on the dates of the siege (39:1-2), the sentence goes on in 39:3: the officers of the king of Babylon came in and sat in the Middle Gate. The words may also be read as closing chapter 38: "and he was there when Jerusalem was captured".

decisions.choice: Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard
decisions.reason: The line of verse 13 returns (37:21). He stayed there until the Babylonians took him out and handed him over to Gedaliah son of Ahikam (39:14).

decisions.choice: This is what happened when (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the closing words a complete sentence that points ahead to chapter 39 (m1); Literal leaves it open as the Hebrew does.
